subject: Clarify rolling maintenance window & response SLAs for Q4 order form
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme-analytics.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Oct 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft order form — maintenance window question

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

Thanks for the updated order form (attached). A couple items popped up in our procurement review that we need to lock before legal will sign:

- The maintenance window language currently allows a 6-hour weekly window. Our SRE prefers no single weekly window over 2 hours for production clusters. Can Redwood propose a rolling weekly maintenance model or narrower window?
- The SLA table references "availability credits" but doesn't define threshold for partial-credit events (e.g., degraded throughput vs full outage). Can we get explicit definitions?
- Response times: procurement wants guaranteed P1 acknowledgement within 30 minutes; we see 1 hour in your draft.

We attached Acme_OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf with inline comments. Could we get proposed redlines for the SLA section and a short note from ops describing operational impact of a rolling schedule vs fixed window?

Best,
Emily Chen
Procurement Lead, Acme Analytics
(emily.chen@acme-analytics.com)

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Oct 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form — maintenance window question

Emily — thanks for the clear list. We appreciate the visibility into Acme's SRE constraints. Quick plan from our side:

1) Marissa (sales) will propose alternative SLA wording that clarifies availability credit bands and the P1 ack target.
2) Aditya (ops) will write a short operational note about rolling maintenance vs fixed windows and the tradeoffs for latency and KV-cache priming.
3) Dev (legal) will look at the redlines for any contractability issues and call out anything that needs legal signoff.

Will circle back with a consolidated redline by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
(tessa_morgan@redwood.com)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Oct 2025 13:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form — maintenance window question

Emily — attaching a short draft with proposed SLA language and a clean table for credits (see SLA_proposed_language.docx). Highlights:

- Availability bands: 99.95% (no credit), 99.5–99.95% (5% monthly credit), 99.0–99.5% (15% credit), <99.0% (30% credit). These are monthly measurement windows.
- P1 acknowledgement moved to 30 minutes; P1 resolution target kept at 4 hours (we'll add escalation path).
- Maintenance: propose a rolling 2-hour weekly maintenance per region, by default scheduled on Tuesdays 00:00–06:00 UTC but eligible for rolling offset up to +/- 72 hours with 72-hour notice for production workloads. When rolling, we guarantee no single customer impact window >2 hours unless mutually agreed.

Open question for ops/legal: the rolling-offset clause needs an explicit statement about performance degradation vs full outage to determine credit triggers.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial — Redwood Inference
(marissa_cole@redwood.com)

Attachments: SLA_proposed_language.docx

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Oct 2025 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form — maintenance window question

Emily / team — quick ops note on the proposed rolling 2-hour window:

- From an implementation standpoint we can do rolling offsets that shift maintenance across days for shards/instances to limit per-customer impact. This requires a coordinated runbook and a pre-warm step for KV cache to avoid cold-start latency spikes.
- If Acme needs strict guarantee that no single customer sees >2 minutes of elevated latency during maintenance, that's much harder (would require temporary routing and double-serving for all affected regions). We can support the Garbled-peak protection pattern but that will add complexity and likely a 10–15% cost delta on those instances.
- Suggested compromise: Redwood provides rolling 2-hour per-region maintenance. During maintenance we classify impacts as:
  * "Degraded" — higher latency or reduced throughput; does not trigger full outage credit unless latency exceeds X ms for Y minutes.
  * "Unavailable" — no responses; triggers outage credit per SLA table.

I'll draft a one-page runbook and attach. For now, I recommend we keep the P1 ack at 30 minutes and add the precise thresholds for degraded vs unavailable (e.g., 95th pct latency > 800ms sustained for 10 mins triggers degraded).

—Aditya
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference
(aditya_rao@redwood.com)

Attachments: maintenance-runbook.pdf

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme-analytics.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acme-analytics.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2025 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form — maintenance window question

Thanks all — this is helpful and closer to what procurement and SRE need. A few next items from our side:

- Acme accepts the P1 ack change to 30 minutes.
- We need explicit numeric thresholds for "degraded" vs "unavailable" in the SLA redline before legal signs. Can you please insert the suggested 95th-pct numbers and minute thresholds into the SLA_proposed_language.docx and return?
- Procurement also asks that the rolling-offset clause include a maximum number of consecutive rolling shifts per quarter (Acme proposes no more than 2 consecutive rolling shifts for the same time-of-day to avoid operational surprises).

If you can send updated redlines + DocuSign link end of day Monday we should be able to route to legal the same week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Emily Chen
Procurement Lead, Acme Analytics
(emily.chen@acme-analytics.com)
